transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date: 2026-01-10
- Start: 14:30 UTC
- Duration: ~62 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Kaito Tanaka (Kairo Head of Platform), Priya Rao (ML Eng), Samir Patel (CTO)

Auto-generated Summary (brief):
Redwood and Kairo aligned on POC goals: characterize real production traffic (QPS, concurrency, token mix), define benchmark scenarios (steady, burst, long-tail), agree on success criteria for latency at p95/p99 and throughput. Action: SE to deliver harness, customer to share 72h sample, schedule pilot kickoff week of 2026-01-20.

Topics: workload geometry, QPS/concurrency, input/output token distribution, tail latency SLAs, deployment mode (Dedicated vs Private), security gating (KMS/SAML/SOC2).

Action Items (captured live): see metadata action_items field above.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex Lee: alright everyone, thanks for joining. quick kickoff — we wanted to scope the POC around your traffic shape and what success looks like.
[00:00:12] Kaito Tanaka: yep thanks. we, um, we are trying to replace an internal inference service and want predictable cost and tail latency, particularly during funding rounds when traffic spikes.
[00:00:28] Maya Chen: great. before we jump into numbers: can you confirm current infra and where inference runs, e.g., k8s on gcp, any VPC peering, and whether data must stay in a VPC or on prem?
[00:00:40] Priya Rao: it's GCP GKE with a private VPC. we have VPC pairing to partner services — sorry, peering. we also have a KMS (cloud KMS) for keys and need audit logs forwarded.
[00:00:53] Samir Patel: and SOC2 in flight, probably will ask for a copy of Redwood's compliance pack.
[00:01:02] Alex Lee: noted, we'll send SOC2 summary and security whitepaper. Maya, can you take the traffic questions?
[00:01:08] Maya Chen: sure. Priya, rough current QPS and burst characteristics? numbers help us pick Dedicated pool sizing and requester concurrency.
[00:01:18] Priya Rao: baseline steady is around 1.2k qps across API endpoints, but we see 5k qps spikes for 8-12 minutes when a batch job runs and in the evening a 2x diurnal bump. concurrency observed at the service level peaks around 320 active requests.
[00:01:35] Maya Chen: that's helpful. what's the token distribution? input and output averages and extremes?
[00:01:40] Priya Rao: inputs are small — mean ~48 tokens, median 32, some long prompts up to 800 tokens for advanced analytics. outputs mean ~240 tokens, but there are generative jobs that produce 3k-5k tokens occasionally; 95th at about 800 and 99th at ~2.6k. so heavy right tail.
[00:02:00] Kaito Tanaka: and importantly, we need p95 generation latency < 400ms for interactive queries, p99 < 1.2s for noninteractive is okay but prefer lower. throughput SLA for batch style endpoints — we want throughput not to degrade by more than 30% during bursts.
[00:02:17] Maya Chen: ok that clarifies tradeoffs: low-latency interactive vs cost for long outputs. for the POC we'll propose three benchmark scenarios:
[00:02:25] - steady-state 1.2k QPS for 60 minutes
[00:02:28] - burst test: ramp to 5k QPS for 10 minutes, sustained bursts for 3 separate 10-min windows within an hour
[00:02:35] - long-tail playback: 72-hour compressed replay to surface diurnal and the 99th token-length events
[00:02:42] Maya Chen: we'll run each with the real token distribution you provide plus an instrumented run capturing p50/p95/p99 latency, token-per-second throughput, GPU utilization, and cost estimate delta.
[00:02:51] Priya Rao: are you able to simulate KV cache warm vs cold? some of our endpoint responses reuse prefixes heavily.
[00:02:58] Maya Chen: yes — harness supports three cache modes: cold (no kv), warm (prepopulated prefix cache), and mixed. we can also vary batch sizes and max tokens-per-request to map latency vs cost.
[00:03:08] Samir Patel: curious about model variants: do you have smaller quantized variants we can use as fallback during big bursts? fallback behavior is critical for us.
[00:03:18] Alex Lee: Redwood supports model variants and automated fallback policies; we can route burst traffic to a quantized variant (4-bit or 8-bit) with small quality delta. we'll include quality checks in the harness (BLEU/ROUGE-ish or custom evals you provide).
[00:03:33] Kaito Tanaka: great. security — for Private deployment trial we need KMS-integration and SSO (SAML). can Redwood's pilot run inside our VPC?
[00:03:42] Maya Chen: yes, the Private option supports customer VPC and on-prem package. for pilot we usually do either Dedicated in Redwood cloud with VPC peering or a Private control plane depending on the data sensitivity. we'll send the deployment checklist.
[00:03:55] Priya Rao: about instrumentation: we need token-level counters, per-route cost, and per-request trace ids to reconcile with app logs.
[00:04:03] Maya Chen: included. Redwood Console will give per-route token breakdown, latency percentiles, and you can forward traces to your tracing backend.
[00:04:10] Alex Lee: quick question on success criteria — besides p95/p99 and throughput, what else matters for you to sign off on the POC?
[00:04:17] Kaito Tanaka: stability during bursts (no more than 10% error rate increase), cost predictability (unit cost within 20% of estimate), and no data egress concerns. also a clear rollback path to our old service if quality regressions appear.
[00:04:31] Maya Chen: we'll include an evaluation matrix: latency, error rate, quality delta vs baseline model, cost delta, and operational checklist.
[00:04:39] Priya Rao: timeline? how long to run the benchmark and get results?
[00:04:43] Maya Chen: typical cadence: harness + infra prep (3 business days after we get traffic sample), run benchmark suite (2 days to run all scenarios), analyze results and follow-up (2-3 days). so end-to-end ~10 business days, shorter if you accept a reduced run.
[00:04:58] Alex Lee: proposed pilot: 4-week pilot overall — week 0 prep, week 1 run initial benchmarks, week 2 tuning and canary small production traffic, week 3 extended soak and SLA verification.
[00:05:10] Samir Patel: ok that timeline seems do-able. we need cost numbers though — even a ballpark for Dedicated pool with 320 concurrency baseline and burst headroom to 5k qps.
[00:05:19] Maya Chen: we'll provide a sizing estimate. quick back-of-envelope: if your payloads average 288 tokens total (input+output) and model generates at 30 tokens/sec per GPU thread, we estimate X GPUs for steady; detailed numbers in the sizing doc. we'll send a spreadsheet with multiple quantization and batching options.
[00:05:36] Priya Rao: please include a mode where we prioritize latency (smaller batches) and another where we prioritize cost (larger batch + quantized).
[00:05:43] Maya Chen: absolutely. also we'll instrument prefix cache hit-rate sensitivity so you can see cost benefits of caching.
[00:05:49] Kaito Tanaka: do you have any standard benchmark harness links now? can we look at it?
[00:05:53] Maya Chen: yes sending link now in chat, but we'll follow up by email: https://redwood.ai/poc-harness/kairo (note: internal doc, creds in the email).
[00:06:01] Alex Lee: final recap: Maya sends harness + runbook + compliance pack, Priya shares 72h sample, Kaito confirms security gating. we'll target kickoff week of Jan 20th and aim to produce a full benchmark report within two weeks of the run.
[00:06:15] Priya Rao: one more thing — for the long outputs, can you measure token-level latency (ms/token) and p99 generation throughput? we want to know if insanely long outputs will block GPU threads.
[00:06:25] Maya Chen: yes we'll capture ms/token and per-GPU generation throughput and show per-request tail occupancy.
[00:06:31] Samir Patel: cool. thanks all.
[00:06:34] Alex Lee: thanks everyone. we'll send notes and action items.
